Purpose and exclusions

Record intentionally deferred ideas so they do not silently become dependencies of the first playable RPG. Each requires a separate approved scope and proof before production systems or UI are exposed.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create only DA_ExpansionPolicy_Default with all states Deferred; do not create auction/PvP/housing gameplay shells during early phases.
  2. Hide unavailable UI entries rather than displaying purchase or join actions that cannot work.
  3. Add a content validation rule rejecting an enabled flag without its approval/evidence record.
  4. Retest base-game progress without any optional service so an expansion outage cannot block the original PvE loop.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Deferred expansion gates: PvP, raids, housing, auctions and monetization. Rule owner: URPGExpansionPolicy. This asset’s role is Record intentionally deferred ideas so they do not silently become dependencies of the first playable RPG. Each requires a separate approved scope and proof before production systems or UI are exposed.

  1. PvP requires consent/rules, authority, lag/hit fairness, anti-abuse and separation of PvE balance before player damage can activate.
  2. Raids require measured larger encounters, group credit/loot recovery and readable 2D telegraphs; the four-player dungeon does not prove raid scale.
  3. Housing requires persistent placement limits, ownership/permissions, moderation, storage/instance lifecycle and sourced 3D art.
  4. Auction requires durable escrow, pricing/fees, expiry/returns, offline fulfillment, dupe-resistant settlement and economy operations; direct safe trade comes first.
  5. Monetization requires a separate ethical/legal/platform/payment/refund/fraud/privacy review with verified current requirements; no payment endpoints, premium currency or storefront are committed here.
  6. Leave all expansion flags disabled. A reviewed ADR and acceptance evidence must precede integration into the production catalog.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: Architecture review only; no active production map fixture. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Unapproved flag enabled -> release validation failure.
Client sends PvP damage request with flag disabled -> UnsupportedAction and no player health change.
Auction service absent -> inventory and direct merchants/trades still work.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
